R.S. 18:1283(A) says an election that the Constitution or a law requires 'as a prerequisite to the issuance of bonds, levying or increasing of any tax, or the assumption of indebtedness' is held under Chapter 6-A's procedures. R.S. 18:1281 says Chapter 6-A 'shall apply to and shall supersede' older procedure provisions, 'notwithstanding any contrary provisions contained therein'. notes: All 870 questions were placed by TITLE only: questions.json has no 'subject' or 'text' (ballot wording) for any question, so every kind below is read from the title (and the date/county in the id where noted). Each rule carries 'match_regex' (Python, case-insensitive, applied to the title) and 'question_ids'; a question belongs to the first rule in file order whose match applies, so the rules partition the 863 questions covered. 7 questions are in kinds_not_covered.

Every threshold found is a simple majority of the votes cast on the question (t = 0.5). 'Exactly half is not a majority': all the quoted provisions say 'majority' (or, for referenda generally, G.S. 163-182.15(d), that the proposal with the highest number of votes prevails); a tie carries nothing. No quoted provision sets a turnout floor, a share of registered voters, or a supermajority for any listed kind. The only compound conditions found are the multicounty-district rule for Article 43 transportation districts (G.S. 105-509.1, 105-510.1) and the service-district concurrent-majority rule for bonds (G.S. 153A-308, 160A-543); both are written in the 'compound' fields and apply only in those settings.

Fetching: all pages were fetched with curl -sSL from www.ncleg.gov, one request every six seconds or more, no refusals (every page returned 200). WebFetch was not used. WebSearch was used three times only to look for session-law numbers; nothing in the rules is taken from a search result, only from pages saved in /tmp/vote-cache/law-local/NC/pages/. The saved folder also holds whole-chapter pages (Chapters 18B, 69, 105, 115C, 153A, 159, 160A, 163 from /EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/ByChapter/) used to find the sections, and the session-law index pages (https://www.ncleg.gov/Laws/SessionLaws/<year>) used to find local acts. Justia and Cornell LII were not needed.

Quotes: each 'quote' was checked by script as an exact substring of the saved page's text after tags were removed and runs of whitespace (including the line breaks in the session-law pages) were collapsed to one space. '[...]' marks a cut. Every 'also_cited' quote was checked the same way.

Dates of the text: the code pages are the current text as fetched on 2026-11-07 (their history lines are on each page). For the 2008-2010 quarter-cent sales tax questions and the 2008 land transfer tax questions the 2007 enacting text was also read (S.L. 2007-323, s. 31.17, saved as SL2007-323.html) and has the same sentence, so no from_year/to_year is given for the sales tax rules. The land transfer tax article (G.S. 105-600 to 105-604, Art. 60) was repealed by S.L. 2011-18 effective 2011-03-31; the current code page shows only 'Repealed', so that rule is read from S.L. 2007-323 and carries from_year 2007, to_year 2011. For the other statutes cited the history lines show amendments (e.g. G.S. 159-61 by 2013-200 and 2023-134 on ballot wording; G.S. 18B-602 by 2021-150; G.S. 160A-209 by 2022-62, s. 47; G.S. 153A-149 by 2022-62 and 2023-107) but the page does not show whether the threshold sentence itself changed; the sentences quoted are the ones now in force. The subsection letters quoted (e.g. 160A-209(e), 153A-149(d)) are the current ones and may differ for older questions.

G.S. 163-182.15(d) ('In a referendum, the ballot proposal receiving the highest number of votes shall be declared to have prevailed') is the only general referendum result rule read. The page does not show when that sentence was added; it is used only as support for the mixed beverage, ABC store, alcohol-unnamed and Asheville water rules, all marked inferred.

Alcohol: G.S. 18B-602(b) and (e) state the majority test for malt beverage and unfortified wine propositions. For ABC store and mixed beverage elections the Article states only the ballot words (18B-602(g), (h)); the threshold is read from 18B-601(a), 18B-604(b)-(c) and 163-182.15(d), so those two rules are 'inferred'. Township elections (Lee, Moore, Harnett, etc.) are decided 'in the same manner as county elections' (G.S. 18B-600(f)).

Local sales and use tax referendums: Articles 43 and 46 call the referendum 'advisory' in the text but tie the board's power to levy to the majority vote of those voting; the share needed is the same in Articles 39, 43 and 46. The title alone does not say which Article a question was held under, except 'QUARTER' (Article 46) and 'PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION' (Article 43). A tax defeated by the voters can also be levied by the board without an election after five years (G.S. 105-466(b), Article 39); that is not a vote threshold.

Local acts: 18 questions were matched by name and date to a local act that was fetched and read (Pink Hill S.L. 2011-46, Kinston 2011-67, Reidsville 2011-139, Oak Island 2011-51, Rougemont 2011-114, Castle Hayne 2011-166, Sneads Ferry 2009-431, Tobaccoville 2016-43, Alexander County board of education 2023-41, Rowan-Salisbury board of education 2024-2, Greene County 2011-169, Caswell County zoning 2020-22, Hatteras pathway 2017-50 (matched by subject word and county only, marked inferred), Durham prepared food tax 2008-116, Indian Trail and Stallings occupancy taxes 2023-144 (4 questions)). All use 'a majority of the votes cast' (or 'of those voting'), except the Caswell zoning referendum, which is advisory and sets no threshold (t = null). The other charter amendment, board of commissioners structure, and fire/property tax questions could have been put under a local act instead of the general law cited; the acts for those were not located or read, so those rules are inferred.

Rowan-Salisbury board of education (S.L. 2024-2, s. 5(b)): 'If the majority of the qualified voters of Rowan County vote in favor of the referendum' could be read as a majority of all qualified voters rather than of those voting. The act does not say 'of all registered voters'; the sister act for Alexander County (S.L. 2023-41, s. 4) says 'the majority of the votes cast'. t = 0.5 of those voting is used; the other reading is flagged here, not applied.

N.C. Const. art. V as fetched shows S.L. 2026-4 and 2026-5 amendments to sections 2(5) and 2(6) 'contingent upon the results of the November 3, 2026, referendum'. They do not touch the 'majority of the qualified voters of the unit who vote thereon' wording in sections 2(5) and 4(2). Whether that referendum has passed is not on the page.

Bonds: G.S. 159-49 puts every bond that needs a vote under the Local Government Bond Act, and 159-61(a) sets the test. The constitution (art. V, sec. 4(2)) sets the same majority for pledging a unit's faith and credit. A bond a unit may issue without a vote (G.S. 159-49 exceptions, revenue bonds) would not appear as a ballot question. The sentence in 159-61(a) reads 'the affirmative vote or a majority' in the code (apparently a slip for 'of'); the quote keeps the code's own words.

The 'Greensboro City Council Four-Year T' question and the Mecklenburg 'Board of Commissioners 4 Year Terms' question are term-length changes, which are optional forms under G.S. 160A-101(4) and 153A-58(2); they are placed under the matching general vote rule (inferred).
